newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile shrs rebound at close, drought fears subside.
newsitem.headline: Chile shrs rebound at close, drought fears subside.

text.p: Capping a three-day losing streak, Chilean blue chips closed sharply higher as investors realised they had overreacted to government measures announced Monday to control electricity demand, said traders.
The bolsa is seen opening calmer as the market pauses for breath after the roller-coaster sessions, they said.
"I see no reason for the market to rise, unless extra foreign money comes in," said Marco Antonio Vargas, vice president for equity research at Merrill Lynch.
The 40-share .IPSA index ended up 1.6 percent at 117.92 points.
The general index gained 0.81 percent at 5,364.25 points amid turnover of 13.8 billion pesos.
The rally was driven by rises in Chilean-issued ADRs which climbed on the back of Wall Street's surge.
Electricity stocks, which have been badly hammered this week, rose as players realized the measures may hurt company profits as badly as they had been expecting.
The government imposed the restrictions as this year's drought -- the worst in Chile this century -- has slashed power output from hydroelectric generators.
Chilgener climbed 4.42 percent to 171-1/4 pesos, while Endesa rallied 2.43 percent to 253 pesos.
Once fears over the drought receded, the market was able to turn its eyes to the Central Bank's interest rate cut which was announced after market's closed Friday.
"No-one had time to digest the rate cut. People weren't expecting it so soon," said Vargas.
Losers included forestry firm Masisa, down 2.65 percent at 220 pesos and drug-maker LabChile which shed 2.3 percent to 425 pesos.
